text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the weakness or numbness follow a specific pattern, such as affecting the thumb and index finger versus the ring and little fingers? I need to determine if this suggests a single nerve root compression or a more distal peripheral neuropathy.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fasciculations and absent reflexes suggests lower motor neuron involvement, which is concerning for cervical myelopathy or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of a cervical syrinx, combined with your history of trauma and lower motor neuron signs, confirm the diagnosis of Syringomyelia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
